Age Identity (X25519 secret key). Possessing it decrypts all ciphertext encrypted to the corresponding recipient.
Coinbase Access Token bearer token validated against api.coinbase.com/v2/user; likely grants trading permissions — full account takeover.
Coinbase CDP API Key (ECDSA): captures org key name + raw EC private key PEM. Can sign all CDP transactions.
Coinbase CDP API Key (Ed25519): captures key UUID + raw 64-byte Ed25519 private key. Same full-signing impact as ECDSA variant.
MD5crypt ($1$). MD5 cracks at billions/sec on GPU; high recovery probability depending on password strength.
bcrypt ($2a/b/x/y$). Designed to be slow; cost factor makes cracking expensive. Short/common passwords still at risk.
SHA256crypt ($5$). Stronger than md5crypt with configurable rounds; standard in Linux shadow. Moderate cracking resistance.
SHA512crypt ($6$). Better digest than sha256crypt; common in modern Linux shadow files. Moderate resistance.
Cisco IOS PBKDF2-SHA256 ($8$). Strong KDF but success yields network device admin — elevated impact context.
1Password Service-Account Token (ops_eyJ...) unlocks all vaults accessible to the service account — master key for stored credentials.
1Password Account Secret Key. One of two auth factors; alone insufficient, but combined with weak/reused master password enables full takeover.
Generic PEM private key (RSA/DSA/OPENSSH/EC). Full unencrypted private key — identity impersonation, TLS decryption, anything the cert trusts.
Base64-double-encoded PEM private key (Kubernetes-style). Decodes to identical impact as np.pem.1; extra encoding layer is not a security control.
Encrypted RSA private key (Proc-Type: 4,ENCRYPTED). Passphrase provides partial protection; weak/nearby passphrases likely. Low-end critical.
Broad PEM private key (RSA/PGP/DSA/OPENSSH/ENCRYPTED/EC). Unencrypted key material for all major types; full signing/decryption capability.
WireGuard PrivateKey. Enables full peer impersonation on VPN; decrypt all tunneled traffic, access entire private network segment.
WireGuard PresharedKey. Weakens quantum-resistance layer but does not alone break the tunnel — peer private key still required for handshake.
